title: Hyundai Accused of Leaving Transport Operators Without Routes and Putting More Than 300 Jobs at Risk
author: Bertha Becerra
content:
_This article by[Bertha
Becerra](https://oem.com.mx/elsoldemexico/analisis/autor/bertha-becerra-1236)
originally appeared in the [September 13, 2026 edition of El Sol de
México](https://oem.com.mx/elsoldemexico/mexico/hyundai-senalada-por-dejar-
sin-rutas-a-transportistas-y-poner-en-riesgo-mas-de-300-empleos-32065130)._

The Korean automaker Hyundai de México intends to dismantle its main logistics
provider of more than a decade, Transportista Kamu, S. de R.L., and leave
**more than 300 transport workers** without jobs, in order to fake a
bankruptcy. And all to evade compliance with the Remediation Plan of the T-MEC
Rapid Response Labor Mechanism (RRLM), for violating freedom-of-association
rights.

So denounced today Jesús Iturbero, general secretary of the Supply Chain
Transport Workers Union (SITRABICS), who said that since January of this year,
the commitments Hyundai made have not been honored.

"This process is moving forward with serious difficulties, due to the
persistent denial of this right and to reprisals by the company against
workers who join or express sympathy for SITRABICS," he told El Sol de México.

He revealed that "this situation is aggravated by the company's obstinate
conduct of failing to comply with national labor, social-security, and tax
laws, and pressuring its transport operators to engage in illegal unfair-
competition practices in the United States, by demanding that its workers
perform cabotage under threat of reprisal and with the high risk that **ICE
will take away their work visas**."

Faced with this grave situation, the general secretary of SITRABICS demands
that the Secretariat of Labor and Social Welfare (STPS), the IMSS, and the SAT
establish a Tripartite Negotiating Table. And that it include Hyundai
executives to halt the dismantling of the operation of Transportación Kamu, S.
de R.L. de C.V. and protect employment in Mexico.

As well as taking measures to reactivate the work of the transport operators
and guarantee the comprehensive remediation ordered by the T-MEC RRLM since
January, of the collective rights of the SITRABICS workforce.

## Unfair Competition Practices

He explained that drivers of the Kamu company, which depends on Hyundai, are
made to sign for cargo destined for Mexico, when in reality it is going to
Texas or other states of the American Union. At customs, when the paperwork
and shipments are reviewed and do not match, they take away their visa, sue
them, deport them, and they can no longer work.

"That's how the pressure works. And many accept the risk," said the general
secretary of SITRABICS.

> In our union, at least 5 members no longer have their visa to work as
> transport operators in the United States.

And those who do not accept these types of cabotage trips are left in the
United States without pay for up to a week.

He highlighted that on Thursday, September 3, the transport drivers and owners
of the cargo trucks shut down the border crossing in Mexicali to demand the
return of their visas.

## They Demand a Response From the Secretariat of Governance

He demanded a response from the Secretariat of Governance on this serious
problem. **" I sent a document with all the information to Secretary Rosa
Icela Rodríguez. It is a very serious problem all along the border strip. The
Foreign Relations Secretariat and the Secretariat of Labor must also
intervene,"** he specified.

In the course of the interview, Mr. Jesús Iturbero stated that in this complex
context, the company Hyundai Glovis America, based in Irvine, California, the
main client of Transportista Kamu S. de R.L. de C.V., at the beginning of
August behaved as follows:

> It left dozens of transport operators without route assignments in the U.S.,
> and without income, in a maneuver of operational asphyxiation.

"That is, without assigning them export routes for delivering supplies from
Mexico to the vehicle production plant in Montgomery, Alabama, United States."

And it turns out that Transportista Kamu, which belongs to Hyundai, accuses
SITRABICS of being to blame for the lack of supply transport to Hyundai. But
this paralysis occurred in parallel to the complaint process before the T-MEC
RRLM, which the SITRABICS union filed with the binational labor authorities,
Mexico and the United States, he pointed out.

"It was in the framework of demanding compliance with the Remediation Plan
that obliges the company to act in accordance with the law and respect freedom
of association," the union leader Iturbero emphasized.

He explained that both Kamu, the transport company, and Hyundai, the
automaker, use the **" swallow company" (_empresa golondrina_) strategy.**
Thus, while Kamu keeps its workers in the yards without collecting full wages,
Hyundai began to progressively transfer export routes, apparently to other
transport companies.

And with that, to gradually reduce the fleet of trucks, to simulate asset
shortfalls at its contractor of more than eleven years, to fake a bankruptcy
and evade the payments to workers stipulated by the Federal Labor Law.

"This is **grave harm to the workers.** And at the Federal Labor Center of
Tijuana (CFLT), there is no support because Kamu's administrators greet the
federal Labor officials 'with hugs and kisses,' and with that they intimidate
the transport operators. They buy off any authority."

The workers are pressured to give in. They have told him:

> I had to sign, I had no other choice!

He also commented that **" I have already informed Dr. Gabriel Tamariz, of the
Secretariat of Labor and Social Welfare, about these situations and about the
grave risk of simulation by a company like Hyundai, with which SITRABICS has
more than a decade of work."**

He affirmed: "We consider it urgent that actions be taken against the
multinational company Hyundai, including its subsidiary Hyundai México, S.A.
de C.V., so that it assumes the legal responsibilities of its supply chain,
after benefiting directly for more than a decade from the services of this
labor fleet."
